title: Check yourself: Hub and spoke: what the coordinator owns

questions.stem: A coordinator spends ten turns locating the broken check and its failure text, then tells a subagent only to "fix the broken check". The subagent opens other modules and edits the wrong one. What should the coordinator have done?

options.text: Write the path, the message and its decisions into the prompt it hands over
options.says: The subagent's context starts fresh, so the brief is the only channel for facts the coordinator already found.

options.text: Rely on the subagent to inherit the parent's earlier tool results by itself, unprompted
options.says: Ruled out because nothing is inherited: "The only content you pass from parent to subagent is the Agent tool's prompt string".

options.text: Name a stronger model for the subagent in its definition file
options.says: Ruled out because the problem is missing information, and "a vague brief produces vague work."

options.text: Add a line telling the subagent to ask the coordinator whenever it is unsure
options.says: Ruled out because the subagent cannot converse with its parent while it runs: "only its final message returns to the parent".

origin.section: Hub and spoke, and where the context goes

questions.stem: A team plans a multi-agent design for a feature whose planning, coding and verifying steps all draw on the same evolving sources, with the user steering between steps. Which choice fits best?

options.text: Run the three steps as parallel subagents to cut the total waiting time
options.says: Ruled out because a delegate loses time: a subagent that is not a fork "starts fresh and may need time to gather context".

options.text: Give each step to its own subagent
options.says: Ruled out because the documentation lists this case for the main conversation: "multiple phases share significant context, such as planning, implementation, and testing".
The steps depend on one shared context and on steering, which a team cannot give.

options.text: Add a coordinator that merges what the three step-agents produce at the end
options.says: Ruled out because the dependencies are the problem: "some domains that require all agents to share the same context or involve many dependencies between agents are not a good fit".

origin.section: When the coordinator should not delegate at all
